text:
maria: quick sync — we need to pick the runtime plumbing for smart routing policy evals. Options: sidecar service, in-process library, or wasm sandbox. Goals: p50 decision <2ms, explainability string on each decision, hot-reload without restarts, easy sim/shadowing for rollout. thoughts?

jake: sidecar = isolation + hot reload, easier to run different versions per-host. downside: RPC cost (~0.5-1ms if localhost unix socket), and backpressure if the evals block. still my +1 for initial rollout. :+1:

anika: library = fastest path (no rpc) but couples runtime to product process. version skew and safety are real concerns (one bad policy can crash). ops surface increases.

leo: wasm sandboxing looks attractive — isolation + lighter-weight than a separate service. usability concerns: debugging and tooling, plus need to measure serialization costs for request/response.

jake: wasm (wasmtime, host-call): median 1.6ms, p95 3.2ms

jake: quick numbers from yesterday's bench (simple rule set):
```
library: median 0.34ms, p95 0.85ms
sidecar (gRPC local): median 0.95ms, p95 1.8ms
wasm (wasmtime, host-call): median 1.6ms, p95 3.2ms
```
so library wins perf; sidecar is OK for most routes; wasm needs tuning but gives safety.

anika: we also need strong explainability attached to each decision (human-readable "why" + rule id + provenance). telemetry: per-decision trace id so we can replay in sim. and TTL for cached decisions.

maria: proposal: hybrid approach: default to in-process library for hot path (low-latency), sidecar for experimental/complex policies + policy hot-reload, wasm for tenant-provided or untrusted logic. migration via shadowing and sim-first. fallback: when new evals exceed error/latency thresholds, auto-fall back to legacy scorer.

leo: agree on hybrid. small checklist for rollout:
- add "policy.mode" config (library|sidecar|wasm) in route config
- sim harness that can run 100% synthetic traffic with historical traces
- shadow mode: decision computed but not used; compare deltas and log explainability
- canary: 10% traffic -> 50% -> 100% with automatic rollback if error rate > 0.5% or latency spike > 20%

policy-bot: sim results uploaded to http://ci.redwood/sim/1768 (shadow vs legacy). overall mismatch rate 0.8% on small sample; majority due to recent penalty tweak.

anika: two important infra concerns we must call out in RFC: cache invalidation semantics (per-tenant key + versioned policy key) and determinism requirements for sim (no non-deterministic host-time decisions). also service-level contracts: if sidecar unavailable, library must have fallback path (local simple heuristic).

jake: example minimal DSL snippet for explainability & stable serialization — put in RFC: 
```
route_policy v1 {
  rule "prefer-dedicated-eu" {
    when region == "eu" && latency < 120
    then choose { tier: "dedicated", weight: 0.8 }
    explain "prefers EU dedicated when fast"
  }
}
```
this attaches rule id + explain string so sim and telemetry can map diffs.

maria: good. also need an adapter interface for runtime embedding: a) sync call path for library b) async RPC + batch for sidecar c) hostcall shim for wasm. define same request/response contract (decision, explain[], debug_payload) so ops/console can show unified UI.

ops-bot: note: add tracing hooks (span per-decision) so we can correlate token-level latency with routing decisions.

leo: one more: perf budget table in RFC. propose p50 < 2ms, p95 < 5ms for decision layer. experiments that exceed are routed to canary only.

maria: i'll draft the RFC this afternoon with perf numbers, DSL sketch, adapter contract, canary steps, and migration plan. @anika @jake please drop sim configs and the bench scripts into the RFC PR. thanks! :eyes:
